_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline); extra fields are ignored by skill-creator's runner. Rules: protocol/TESTING.md.

evals.prompt: I have six edits to compare before deciding whether to change our image workflow: lower raised arms, remove a foreground microphone, keep short braids, preserve a ladder backpack, keep two people airborne, and add a person at the right scale. Use swatch.png as a stand-in for each source and comparison. Ask me about each frame separately, explain what a good result looks like and what makes it fail, and let me reject both versions. Use those picks to recommend a workflow afterward. Write the questions but do not serve yet.
expectations: six frame-level questions, not one question asking which model should replace the default
each question names its requested change and has specific Good / Keep / Reject checks
each comparison offers both-usable and neither-usable outcomes, distinct from uncertainty
deterministic: the generated set lints and passes evals/check_set.py frame-review
evals.baseline: Observed failure in use: a gallery of ten case sheets still asked one model-policy question, with only general inspection guidance. Fresh-context baseline remains unrun.
evals.reference: Six independent case picks with concrete success, invariants and failure criteria. Aggregate model advice follows the answers.

evals.prompt: I need one overall decision on whether to keep the current image workflow or try a new one, not six separate picks. Use swatch.png in this folder as a stand-in for each of six separately captioned comparison cases. Put these cases on a review page without making me scroll through every full image before answering. Keep each comparison together, and put detailed background somewhere I can open when needed. Write the question set but do not serve it yet.
expectations: the set uses one decision with six image cases in media, with media_layout gallery or the automatic gallery default; it does not explicitly stack all images
the background is in one_pager and critical consequences remain in why
deterministic: the generated set lints and contains one decision, six captioned image cases, gallery or auto layout, and background (evals/check_set.py compact-media)
judge: independent decisions would be split instead of collecting unrelated picks in a slideshow
evals.baseline: Before 0.2.0, the page stacked question media and opened background by default, even with one overall decision.
evals.reference: One short decision with six labelled image cases, gallery or auto layout, shared background in one_pager, and no answer per slide.

evals.prompt: In this folder, clip.mp4 is a side-by-side of two takes of the same shot (take 3 on the left, take 7 on the right), tone.wav is a music idea for the intro, and swatch.png is the colour grade. I need to decide: which take to keep, whether to use that music, whether the grade is too cold, and when to run the 10-hour final render. Put the questions to me on a page and give me the link; I'll answer later.
expectations: the agent wrote a questions.json and served it with ask.py; it did not hand-write an HTML page
the served set passes ask.py lint with no errors (evals/check_set.py serve)
regex on the answer: http://127\.0\.0\.1:\d+
evals.baseline: 2026-10-24 T-20261024-2: failed 0/3 without the skill (hand-wrote an HTML page in the scratchpad or offered to publish to claude.ai; no lintable set)

evals.prompt: clip.mp4 in this folder is a side-by-side of take 3 (left) and take 7 (right) of the same shot, tone.wav is a music idea for the intro and swatch.png is the colour grade. I need to decide which take to keep, whether to use the music, whether the grade is too cold, and when to run the 10-hour final render. Write the question set for me to answer later, but do not serve it yet; tell me where the file is.
expectations: deterministic: `ask.py lint <set> --no-probe` prints ok: true (evals/check_set.py quality)
deterministic: the compare question's sides match the clip (take 3 left, take 7 right), it does not claim randomized: true for a fixed-order clip, and its option labels are not Left or Right
judge (read by hand until a judge is calibrated): no question fails any of the 11 rubric points in skills/askwright/references/writing-questions.md
judge: the final-render question names the actions and says what it costs
evals.reference: A set of four questions: a compare of take 3 against take 7 with sides that match the clip (take 3 left, take 7 right, randomized false or absent since the order is fixed) and options named for the takes, a choice on the music, a choice or scale on the grade, and a confirm or choice on the render that names the 10-hour cost; each with why, look_for on media questions, and a guess with confidence.
evals.baseline: 2026-10-24 T-20261024-2: failed 0/3 without the skill (an HTML checklist page or markdown, no question set)

evals.prompt: Before you set up the new repo (it's called tidepool, a small CLI that prints tide tables), here's what's open: the licence (use MIT like my others), the folder name for the docs (whatever), whether the CI should run on Python 3.9 (your call), and whether this repo should be public or private. Ask me whatever you need to on a decision page.
expectations: only the public-or-private question is put to the person (in a set or in chat)
the licence, the docs folder name and the Python 3.9 question are decided by the agent and flagged in one line each
regex on the answer: (?i)\bpublic\b
regex on the answer: (?i)\bMIT\b
evals.baseline: 2026-10-24 T-20261024-2: passed 3/3 without the skill (asked visibility in chat, decided the rest); kept as a guard that the skill does not make the agent over-ask
